answer: Each identity is bound to one registered master-blacksmith forge: the smith passes a guild exam, the forge is inspected and entered as one vertex, every piece hallmarked — one forge backs one identity, duplicates rejected. That anchor costs one real smith, 1,800 units plus 180 days of supervised forging; 100 fakes cost 180,000 units, 100 forges and 18,000 smith-days. Cheapest cheat: renting a smith's forge for 1,200 units a season — the lender surrenders the forge backing their own identity — while a copied hallmark fails the assay and mesa iron bought elsewhere fails the stamp match.
